source.title: Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
source.authors: Diggs, G. M. Jr.; Lipscomb, B. L.; O'Kennon, R. J.
source.original_treatment_name: Ziziphus obtusifolia (Hook. ex Torr. & A. Gray) A. Gray
historical_synonyms_documented: Condalia obtusifolia (Hook. ex Torr. & A. Gray) Weberb.

morphology_documented.habit: Densely and rigidly branched thorny shrub to ca. 2 m
morphology_documented.branches: Glaucous gray or whitish waxy bloom on branchlets
morphology_documented.leaves: Small and variable, usually below 4 cm; oblong, elliptic or nearly linear; entire or faintly blunt-toothed, obtuse or notched apex, glabrous, gray-green
morphology_documented.flowers: Small clustered or short axillary racemes, petals ca. 1 mm and falling early
morphology_documented.habitat: Rocky or sandy ground, mainly western Texas

source_scope_note: Genus/key traits explicitly identified; modern secondary evidence separately cited; no unsupported species characters inferred.
unresolved_taxonomy_or_source_notes: 2026 POWO accepts Condaliopsis obtusifolia; 1999 Diggs uses Ziziphus obtusifolia; other sources still recognize Ziziphus, so preserve provenance
Difference from Condalia hookeri: gray-glaucous twigs, petals present, small variable leaves vs non-glaucous branches and petal-less flowers
preservation: Additive file; existing species records, photographs, credits and galleries unchanged
